finding.claim: Caller identity is taken from the client-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header without verification, so any client can impersonate any grant holder and delete or rename their files.
finding.sink: ensure_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') at views.py:17 gating file deletion; is_allowed(g.user, f, 'write') at views.py:25 gating rename

trace.note: before_request hook load_user is registered for every request
g.user is set directly from the client header with no session or token check
is_allowed looks up resource['grants'][user] using the attacker-chosen value
abort(403) only when the grant is absent
file is deleted when the check passes

finding.guards_checked: No code in this repo strips, verifies, or restricts the header to a trusted proxy. Exploitability depends on the deployment: if the app is reachable without a proxy that overwrites this header, the bypass is live. The proxy configuration is not in this repo, so this is a precondition to confirm.

verdict.guard_found: Grant checks at acl.py:5 (is_allowed) and acl.py:8-10 (ensure_allowed, abort(403)) are used at views.py:17 and views.py:25, and both act as intended, but they key on the attacker-supplied g.user, so they do not block impersonation. No code in this repo verifies or strips X-Session-User-Verified (views.py:9-11).
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: views.py:11 sets g.user straight from the header, and acl.py:5 and acl.py:10 then gate delete (views.py:17) and rename (views.py:25) on that value, with no guard in the repo that stops it. Whether a client can reach this app with the header intact depends on a proxy configuration outside this repo that overwrites or strips the header, and that cannot be decided from the code available.

finding.claim: Lookup of the file ID happens before any authorization check, so missing IDs (500 KeyError) and forbidden IDs (403) are distinguishable, letting an unauthenticated caller enumerate which file IDs exist.

trace.note: f = STORE[fid] raises KeyError for an unknown fid, producing a 500
forbidden existing IDs return 403, a different response from the missing case

finding.guards_checked: No existence-hiding or uniform-denial logic. Impact is a boolean existence oracle only, with no content exposure, and requires guessing IDs. Severity LOW.

verdict.guard_found: none. No existence-hiding or uniform-denial logic exists. The only checks are ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10), which raises abort(403) and is not swallowed, and is_allowed at views.py:25, which is tested. Neither runs before the lookup at views.py:16 or views.py:24, and no error handler maps KeyError to 404 in views.py.
verdict.reason: The lookup at views.py:16 (and views.py:24) runs before any authorization check, so an unknown fid raises KeyError and returns 500, while an existing forbidden fid returns 403 via acl.py:10 or views.py:26, letting any caller who can reach the endpoint tell which IDs exist; the claim is accurate, and impact is limited to an existence oracle.
